input.question: Why is this year's flu vaccine so bad?
input.ground_truth: The flu vaccine is ordered based on the strains of flu circulating in the world approximately 6 months in advance of the US flu season to allow time to make the vaccine, distribute it, and administer it. In the time between the moment that the target flu strains were selected for inclusion into the vaccine and now the virus strains mutated and are now different from what is in the vaccine. This is not the first time it has happened and so long as the production cycle is 4-6 months it will continue to happen.

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you and your friends want to play outside, but this year, some sneaky germs (the flu) are trying to make everyone feel sick. Every year, grown-ups make a special medicine (the flu vaccine) to help protect us from those sneaky germs.

But this year, the sneaky germs changed a little bit, like if you wore a different hat than last year. The medicine (vaccine) was made thinking the germs would look the same as before, but they changed a little. So, the medicine doesn’t stop the germs as well as it did before. That’s why some people are getting sick even after getting the shot. It’s not that the medicine is bad on purpose—it’s just that the germs tricked everyone a little bit this year!
